paragraphs.title: Remembering the Creator Before Old Age

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Remember now thy Creator.”
easy.q: Whom does Qohelet tell a person to remember?

answers: In the days of thy youth
Only at the end of life
easy.explanation: The command is given for “the days of thy youth.”
easy.q: When should a person remember the Creator?

easy.explanation: The verse warns that “the evil days come not” before old age arrives.
easy.q: What may come after the days of youth?

answers: Before the difficult days and years arrive
medium.explanation: The verse urges remembrance before the evil days and unpleasant years draw near.
medium.q: Why should a person remember the Creator while young?

answers: I have no desire or enjoyment in them
I have no time in them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a time when the person no longer finds pleasure in those years.
medium.q: What does “I have no pleasure in them” mean in context?

answers: Remember the Creator in youth before the difficult years arrive
medium.explanation: The command to remember the Creator comes before the evil days and unpleasant years.
medium.q: What is the order of thought in the verse?

answers: A person should delay serving God
It is wise to act while strength and opportunity remain
Old age is not part of human life
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes remembering the Creator before difficult years limit a person's ability and pleasure.
challenge.q: What central message comes from the contrast between youth and later years?

answers: There is a limited time before the described change occurs
The words apply only to childhood
challenge.explanation: “While” indicates that the command should be obeyed before the evil days arrive.
challenge.q: What does the word “while” suggest at the beginning of the verse?

answers: Remembering the Creator prevents old age
The command prepares a person spiritually before weakness comes
The command concerns only private memory
challenge.explanation: The verse connects early remembrance with the coming decline of ability and pleasure.
challenge.q: What connection exists between remembering the Creator and the description of the years?

paragraphs.title: The Weakening of the Body in Old Age

easy.explanation: The passage says that the sun, light, moon, and stars are darkened.
easy.q: What happens to the sun, light, moon, and stars in the description?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the keepers of the house shall tremble.”
easy.q: What happens to the keepers of the house?

answers: They cease because they are few
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the grinders cease because they are few.”

answers: He shall rise up at the voice of the bird
The mourners go about the streets
medium.explanation: Rising at the voice of a bird suggests light or troubled sleep.

answers: Ordinary movement or activity becomes difficult
medium.explanation: The image contributes to the description of weakness and reduced strength in old age.
medium.q: What does “the grasshopper shall be a burden” help express in context?

answers: They describe various weaknesses of the body and senses
They describe a journey to a new place
medium.explanation: The images involve dimmed sight, trembling limbs, weakened teeth, troubled sleep, and reduced hearing.
medium.q: How do the images in verses 2–5 work together?

answers: Both describe a change in weather
challenge.explanation: The darkened sun, light, moon, and stars poetically suggest weakened vision.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the darkened lights and old age?

answers: To show caution and vulnerability in weakened old age
To show joy during a journey
challenge.explanation: The images portray an older person as more fearful and vulnerable while moving.
challenge.q: Why are fear of high places and fears in the way mentioned together?

answers: The doors being shut in the streets
The sound of the grinding being low
challenge.explanation: The low sound of grinding indicates that hearing has become weaker.
challenge.q: Which detail most clearly suggests declining hearing?

paragraphs.title: The Fading of Life and Death

answers: The collapse of the body and death
easy.explanation: These broken objects symbolize the ending and collapse of earthly life.
easy.q: What do the images of the cord, bowl, pitcher, and wheel describe?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the dust return to the earth as it was.”
The verse says, “the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”
easy.q: To whom does the spirit return?

answers: The breaking of a vital connection and death
medium.explanation: The loosed cord is one of several images portraying the ending of life.
medium.q: What does the loosed silver cord symbolize?

answers: The spirit returns first, followed by bodily collapse
The body and life fail, followed by the return of dust and spirit
Joy comes first, followed by youth
medium.explanation: The broken objects portray death, and the next verse describes the dust and spirit returning.
medium.q: What is the order of thought in verses 6–7?

answers: Because earthly life and the body pass away
Because nothing in the world is real
medium.explanation: Death and the return of the body to dust emphasize the temporary nature of life.
medium.q: Why does the preacher conclude, “Vanity of vanities”?

answers: The body returns to earth, and the spirit returns to God
The body rises to heaven, and the spirit descends to earth
The body remains in the world, and the spirit disappears
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes the destiny of the dust from that of the spirit.

answers: They present a process of breaking and collapse
They present a process of growth
They present a series of feasts
challenge.explanation: The cord is loosed, the bowl is broken, the pitcher is broken, and the wheel is broken.
challenge.q: How do the four images in verse 6 contribute to the description of death?

answers: The temporary nature of human life
A change to the subject of commerce
Proof that death does not exist
challenge.explanation: The repeated word reinforces the fleeting and limited character of life.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “vanity” after the description of death emphasize?

paragraphs.title: Qohelet's Wisdom and the Words of the Wise

easy.explanation: The verse says that he “still taught the people knowledge.”
easy.q: What did the preacher teach the people?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The preacher sought to find out acceptable words.”
easy.q: What kind of words did the preacher seek to find?

answers: As goads and nails fastened by the masters of assemblies
easy.explanation: The passage compares the words of the wise to goads and firmly fastened nails.
easy.q: How are the words of the wise described?

answers: He taught, gave good heed, sought out matters, and ordered proverbs
He remained silent, hid himself, and forgot
medium.explanation: The verse describes teaching, careful attention, seeking, and setting proverbs in order.
medium.q: What activities did the preacher perform concerning wisdom?

answers: The preacher sought words that were worthwhile and truthful
He sought words that were merely long
medium.explanation: The passage joins acceptable words with writing that was upright and true.
medium.q: What relationship exists between acceptable words and words of truth?

medium.explanation: The verse says they are “given from one shepherd.”
medium.q: From whom are the words of the wise given?

answers: They guide and urge a person forward
challenge.explanation: A goad directs and urges, so the image suggests that wise words motivate and guide.
challenge.q: What does the image of goads teach about the words of the wise?

answers: They show examination and arrangement before writing
They show many books without order
challenge.explanation: The preacher gave good heed, sought out matters, and set proverbs in order before presenting truthful words.
challenge.q: How do careful attention and ordering relate to writing words of truth?

challenge.explanation: Both images portray the words of the wise as powerful, steady, and effective.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by “as goads” and “as nails fastened”?

paragraphs.title: Caution About Many Books and the Practical Conclusion

answers: The making of many books without end
easy.explanation: The verse says, “of making many books there is no end.”
easy.q: What does the preacher warn about?

answers: Fear God and keep his commandments
easy.explanation: The conclusion says, “Fear God, and keep his commandments.”
easy.q: What does the preacher command people to do?

answers: Every work, including every secret thing
Only the words of the wise
easy.explanation: The passage says God will bring every work into judgment, including secret things.
easy.q: What will God bring into judgment?

answers: Much study can produce labor and weariness
medium.explanation: The verse says, “much study is a weariness of the flesh.”
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between many books and weariness of the flesh?

answers: The final summary or practical conclusion
medium.explanation: The phrase introduces the final instruction of the passage.
medium.q: What does “the conclusion of the whole matter” introduce?

answers: It is the whole duty of man
It allows people to avoid learning
It removes the certainty of judgment
medium.explanation: The verse says, “this is the whole duty of man.”
medium.q: Why should people keep God's commandments according to the conclusion?

answers: Much activity does not replace fearing God and keeping his commandments
Many books are the only way to keep the commandments
Study and action have no connection
challenge.explanation: The passage warns about endless study and directs attention to faithful obedience.
challenge.q: What contrast exists between making many books and the practical conclusion?

answers: A person is accountable for deeds hidden from other people
challenge.explanation: God's judgment includes every work and every secret thing, whether good or evil.
challenge.q: What does the judgment of every secret thing imply?

answers: It moves from wisdom and books to fear of God, obedience, and accountability
It denies the importance of truth
challenge.explanation: After discussing wisdom, words, and study, the passage ends with practical obedience and judgment.
challenge.q: How does the ending summarize the earlier ideas?
